sugarcane.title: Sugarcane Leaf Disease AI Diagnosis
sugarcane.subtitle: Upload a sugarcane leaf photo to detect Red Rot, Rust, Mosaic, or Yellow Leaf disease with ICAR-verified remedies.
sugarcane.lowConfidenceMsg: The condition could not be identified with sufficient confidence. Please upload a clearer image or consult an agricultural expert.
sugarcane.uncertainDiagnosisNotice: The AI detected visual patterns resembling this disease, but diagnostic confidence is low. Please take a clearer, close-up photo of the affected leaf in bright natural light, or consult your local agricultural officer before taking drastic chemical measures.

descriptions.Healthy: The sugarcane leaf appears healthy with proper green color and no visible disease symptoms.
descriptions.Mosaic: Sugarcane Mosaic Virus causes contrasting dark and light green patches or stripes along the leaf veins.
descriptions.Red Rot: Red Rot causes leaf yellowing, reddening of internal stalk tissues with white patches, and a sour alcoholic odor.
descriptions.Rust: Sugarcane Rust produces small yellowish spots that turn into elongated reddish-brown pustules on leaf undersides.
descriptions.Yellow: Yellow Leaf Virus causes intense yellowing of the leaf midrib on upper leaves, reducing sugar synthesis.
descriptions.Uncertain: The condition could not be identified with sufficient confidence. Please upload a clearer photo or consult an agricultural expert.

Healthy: Maintain balanced NPK fertilizer application according to crop stage.
Ensure timely irrigation during tillering and grand growth phases.
Inspect crop regularly for early signs of pests or disease.
Mosaic: Rogue out and destroy infected young plants to stop viral spread.
Control aphid vectors using recommended neem-based bio-pesticides.
Avoid taking seed setts from infected fields for next planting cycle.
Red Rot: Uproot and burn infected clumps immediately along with surrounding soil.
Apply Trichoderma viride bio-control agent around root zones.
Do not allow irrigation water to flow from infected fields to healthy fields.
Rust: Ensure adequate field aeration and avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer.
Remove heavily infected lower leaves and burn them.
Apply protective copper/sulfur-based fungicide sprays as advised by local Krishi Bhavan.
Yellow: Provide balanced potash and micronutrient spray (Zinc/Iron) to reduce stress.
Control aphid vectors early in the season.
Mark disease-free healthy clumps for seed collection.
Uncertain: Upload a clearer, well-lit photo focusing closely on affected leaf symptoms.
Ensure the image is taken in bright daylight without harsh shadows.
Consult your local Krishi Bhavan officer for an in-person field diagnostic.

Healthy: Use certified disease-free seed cane (sett treatment).
Maintain proper field drainage to prevent waterlogging.
Mosaic: Plant mosaic-resistant sugarcane varieties (e.g., Co 86032, Co 0238).
Keep field borders clear of wild grass hosts.
Red Rot: Hot water treatment of seed setts (50°C for 2 hours) before planting.
Practice 2-year crop rotation with non-host crops like rice or pulses.
Rust: Maintain proper row spacing (4 to 5 feet) for optimal sunlight and ventilation.
Yellow: Maintain proper soil moisture during hot summer months.
Uncertain: Take multiple photos from different angles if symptoms persist.
